prompt: Rank these moments by how good they are for asking a client for a referral, best first.

task.prompt: Rank these moments by how good they are for asking a client for a referral, best first.

items.label: The project kickoff call, before any work
The day after a production bug caused downtime
The client just told you the launched app cut their support tickets in half
You delivered a milestone on time and the client said thanks

task.explanation: Ask when the client feels the value most; never right after a failure, and kickoff is too early because nothing is proven yet.

prompt: Mark the lines in this referral request that weaken it.

task.prompt: Mark the lines in this referral request that weaken it.

segments.text: Hi Priya, great to see the booking app live and the no-show rate dropping.
Do you know anyone at all who might need anything built?
segments.issue: Too vague: the client cannot think of anyone without a clear profile to match.

segments.text: We work best with clinic groups that still run scheduling on spreadsheets.
If someone comes to mind, I can send a short note you could forward.
We will pay you 50% of the project value for every name you send.
segments.issue: An oversized cash reward makes the intro feel transactional and may breach the client's own policies.

segments.text: Thanks again for a great project.

prompt: A happy client, Marco, introduces you by email to a founder friend, Lena, who is "thinking about building an app".

task.prompt: A happy client, Marco, introduces you by email to a founder friend, Lena, who is "thinking about building an app".

steps.question: How should you reply to the introduction?
options: Send Lena your full price list
Reply only to Marco
Reply-all thanking Marco, move him to BCC, and suggest a short call with Lena
Wait for Lena to reach out first
steps.explanation: Thank the introducer publicly, spare him the thread, and make the next step easy for Lena.

steps.question: Lena's need turns out to be a small website, well below your usual project size. What now?
options: Ignore her
Be honest, help where reasonable, and point her to a good-fit option so Marco's goodwill is protected
Quote your full minimum anyway without explanation
Take it and staff a junior to save time
steps.explanation: How you treat a referral reflects on the referrer; an honest, helpful no keeps the relationship.

steps.question: What do you do with Marco afterwards?
options: Ask him for five more names right away
Send him a discount code
Nothing
Thank him and tell him how it went, without sharing confidential details
steps.explanation: Closing the loop shows respect and makes future introductions more likely.

prompt: Write a short message asking a satisfied client for a referral.

task.prompt: Write a short message asking a satisfied client for a referral.
task.context: Client: Anita, COO of a regional logistics company. Your agency built their driver app and dispatch dashboard; on-time deliveries rose from 82% to 94% in three months. Your best-fit clients are mid-size logistics or delivery firms still dispatching manually.

rubric.label: Anchors on the result
rubric.description: References the concrete outcome (on-time deliveries up) so the ask follows value.

rubric.label: Clear referral profile
rubric.description: Describes the specific kind of company or person to introduce, so Anita can think of a name.

rubric.label: Easy and low pressure
rubric.description: Offers to make the intro effortless (e.g. a forwardable note) and makes it fine to say no.

rubric.label: Warm, concise tone
rubric.description: Reads as personal and brief, not templated or transactional.

task.sampleAnswer: Hi Anita, seeing on-time deliveries go from 82% to 94% has been a highlight of our year, thank you for trusting us with it. We do our best work with mid-size logistics or delivery firms still dispatching by phone and spreadsheet. If a peer comes to mind who is wrestling with that, I would be grateful for an introduction. I can send you a two-line note to forward so it takes you a minute. No pressure at all if nobody fits right now. Thanks again, Sam

prompt: Why do referred leads usually close at a higher rate than cold leads?

options: They are already under contract
They always have bigger budgets
Trust is transferred from the person who referred them
They do not need a proposal
mcq.explanation: The referrer's credibility shortens the trust-building phase, which is the slowest part of a cold sale.

prompt: Which referral ask is most likely to produce an introduction?

options: "Refer us and we'll give you a gift."
"Let me know if you hear of anyone."
"Do you know another clinic owner still booking patients by phone who might want what we built for you?"
"Please share our website with your network."
mcq.explanation: A specific profile tied to the client's own experience lets them think of a real person.

prompt: A referral partner sends several leads, none of which fit your services. What is the best response?

options: Stop talking to the partner
Thank them and clarify your ideal client with a concrete example so future referrals fit
Accept every lead regardless of fit
Pay them anyway to keep them happy
mcq.explanation: Partners refer what they understand; teaching them your ICP improves referral quality without losing goodwill.
